issue.title: gateway: a plugin's in-stream error frame is relayed as data — its code/status never reach routing
issue.body:
## Summary

A provider plugin that returns an OpenAI-compatible stream can end it with an error frame:

```
data: {"error":{"message":"...","type":"upstream_error","code":"upstream_timeout","status":504}}
```

Once the plugin has already sent `200`, that frame is **the only signal it can give** — the HTTP status is spent. Today magpie relays it as ordinary bytes: the account is not rested, the turn is not recorded as failed, and nothing downstream can tell "the model answered" from "the model died halfway".

This is not #3197 / #3346 (the upstream connection died). Here the plugin **deliberately** ended the stream and said why; the information exists and is dropped.

## Where this already works

`internal/gateway/chat.go:1311` — on the **translation** path a Chat reply's `{"error": ...}` is parsed, `filterRefused` pulls out `code` / `status`, and it becomes `Event{Kind: KError, Code, Status}`.

## Where it doesn't

`internal/gateway/gateway.go:3965` — when the provider speaks the client's own protocol (`relay == true`), the reply goes through `s.passthrough(...)`, which tidies and relays bytes. Nothing parses `{"error": ...}` on that path.

Plugin-served models always take it: a plugin's `loader.fetch` returns an OpenAI-compatible `Response`, so client and provider protocol match by construction. For **every** plugin, an in-stream error frame is opaque.

## Two concrete gaps

1. **passthrough ignores the error frame.** No `markUnfit` / rest, no failed-turn accounting — the same account keeps being picked for the same request, and the routing view shows a healthy turn.
2. **`streamFailure()` and `filterRefused()` disagree on the shape.** `internal/gateway/gateway.go:5222` writes `{"error":{"message":...,"type":"api_error"}}` with no `code` / `status`, while the Chat parser at `chat.go:1312` reads exactly those fields. So even magpie's own mid-stream failure frame carries none of the routing signal a plugin frame does.

## Questions

1. Should `passthrough` parse `{"error": ...}` at least to (a) end the stream with the protocol's own terminator and (b) record the failure / rest the account? I understand from #3197 that failover itself is impossible once output has started — I'm not asking for that.
2. Should `streamFailure()` carry `code` / `status` so a client sees the same shape whether the failure came from the plugin or from magpie?
3. If plugin-side codes are meant to be client-only, that belongs in the plugin docs (`HOOKS.md` §7 in the scaffold) — right now the scaffold tells plugin authors to set `status` on the frame, which implies the gateway reads it.

## Repro

Any plugin that ends a stream with an error frame — e.g. a provider whose runtime has a hard per-turn wall clock: the plugin watches the clock, aborts at 285s, and emits `{"error": {..., "code": "upstream_timeout", "status": 504}}`. The client gets a readable message; routing sees nothing.

## Not asking

* Changing the "once output started, no failover" rule — that's a deliberate design and #3197 settles the stream-ending part.
* Anything about pre-first-byte failover, which already works.

comments.body:
Reproduced the part of this that is still live on main, and fixed it on a fork branch: `fix/4855-relay-error-frame` (skygunner/magpie, head `5d2adb0fa`, based on `main` at `8abdf53a8`).

**What main already does** (checked with wire-level fakes, kept as is): the frame is relayed byte for byte under the 200, the turn is recorded as failed in Recent calls / Routing / Usage (the frame's message and its `type`/`code` as ErrType), and the account does rest — e68327b217 ("an error carried in a 200 fails as its own status would", Oct 28) landed that side after the report's line numbers were taken. So gap 1's "no failed-turn accounting" is already untrue.

**What was still broken — the title's claim**: the frame's own `status`/`code` members are never read. Every classifier guessed a status from the error message's *words* (`streamStatus`). Concretely, on bare main:

- your exact frame (`code:"upstream_timeout"`, `status:504`, mid-reply): the rest row read `Status: 200`, `Error: "OK: the upstream timed out"` — the failure rested as `other` under an "OK" status line;
- a terse frame naming 429 (`message:"busy"`) failed as `other` at a word-guessed 502, not as a rate limit;
- the same frame as the stream's first event failed the try at the guessed 502 (`errorReply` even decodes the `status` member already and still returns the guess).

**Fix**

- One reader, `namedStatusOf`: the status an error object names on a member of its own — a number 400–599, `status` first, `code` second (Gemini's OpenAI-compatible relays carry theirs as `code`); a string code is not a status.
- Named before guessed wherever the raw frame is in hand: a held stream's error event, a whole 200 body that is only an error, a carried error (`carriedStatus`), and a reply already streaming — the sniffer notes the named status on the try (an `X-Magpie-` note header the client never sees), and the routing loop and `restAfter` fail and rest the turn at it.
- Your Q2: magpie's own Chat failure frame now carries `code` and `status` beside its message, the same shape a plugin's frame has (`streamFailure`).
- An error naming no status reads exactly as before.

**Verification**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `TestRelayStreamErrorFrameSaysItsStatus` on base `8abdf53a8` | FAIL: mid-reply rest at Status 200/"OK: …", terse 429 as `other`, first-event try at 502 |
| the same with the change | green: 504 rests as `other` saying "Gateway Timeout", 429 as `rate`, first-event try/route/usage at 504; frame still relayed byte for byte |
| `TestRelayStreamErrorFrameWithoutStatusAsBefore` | green on both — a frame naming no status reads as before |
| neighbors (stream accounting, passthrough/severed, rest/failure/fallback/refusal/rate/quota, gemini compat, gather, plugins) | 724 pass, 1 pre-existing red (`TestServeWSLListensBesideLoopback`, environment, red on bare main here too) |
| `count=3`, `-race`, `gofmt`, `go vet -tags nogui` (native/linux/windows), `go build` | pass |

**Not verified**: a real plugin over the gateway — the wire-level fakes reproduce your frames; the gathered path (a non-streaming client behind a streaming plugin) still word-guesses, unchanged. On your Q3: I found no HOOKS.md scaffold in magpie or in the community plugins repo as checked out here, so there was nothing to align; if it lives elsewhere, the reader now honors what it tells authors to set.

This is a fork branch, ready for review, not a claim on the issue's ownership.

## 我这边的状态：能补的正好是「真实插件验证」这一项

看了 `@skygunner` 的 `fix/4855-relay-error-frame`（`5d2adb0fa`），他自己划的两条边界都合理：fork 分支待评审、没在真实插件上验过。

补一句我这边的条件 —— `magpie-magicrew-auth` 走的就是插件流式转发，帧形状和他复现的一致（上游在 **HTTP 200 的 SSE 里**回 `{"code":…,"message":…}`，不是非 2xx）。所以「真实插件跑一遍、看 `code/status` 有没有真的进路由」这件事我这边能补，不需要 wire-level fake。

具体两条路，看你们哪条方便：

1. **分支 rebase 到当前 main / 开个 PR**，我拉下来在本机跑一轮：用 magicrew 两个站各发一次会被上游拒的请求，把 trace 里 `fail` 前后对照贴回来。
2. 或者先不动代码：告诉我你想要的帧样例，我用插件构造同样的帧先确认 `namedStatusOf` 能读到 `status`/`code`，再等你合。

不着急，但这条别烂尾 —— 缺的恰恰是「帧自带的 status 到不了路由」这一步的**实测**，而不是又一个 fake。

Live-plugin frames, as promised — no fakes.

From this machine's usage log (137,771 calls since 10-24), 145 calls came back `200` with a non-empty `err`. Of those, **32 are an upstream error frame that arrived inside a 200 SSE stream** — every one of them `wps-lingxi/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, and every one recorded as a served call:

- 19 × `灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：我还在不断学习中…（请求或内容有问题，重试无效）（HTTP 502）`
- 3 × `灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：…（上游审核未通过）（HTTP 502）`
- 3 × `灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常（上游暂时不可用，可重试）（HTTP 503）`
- 2 × `灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常`
- 3 × `灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：…` (no status named)

Three of the latest, verbatim:

```
2026-11-04T18:29:11  wps-lingxi/deepseek-v4.1-flash  status=200  ms=9583  err=灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：…（HTTP 502）
2026-11-04T18:46:44  wps-lingxi/deepseek-v4.1-flash  status=200  ms=3173  err=灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常（上游暂时不可用，可重试）（HTTP 503）
2026-11-04T18:46:47  wps-lingxi/deepseek-v4.1-flash  status=200  ms=3582  err=灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常（上游暂时不可用，可重试）（HTTP 503）
```

**What routing sees:** a served call. The 502/503 exists only in the plugin's error text — no `fail` entry, no failover, no backoff. The two 503s are six seconds apart and both went to the same model, which is the concrete shape of “the frame's status never reaches routing”.

**The other 101 rows are not this bug.** They are magpie's own guards (`magpie ended this reply: the model's reasoning was stuck in a loop…`) — I am separating them out so the count is not flattered.

**If the raw bytes are what you need:** the wps-lingxi plugin is third-party (`providers-aaaa/magpie-wps-lingxi`). Say the word and I will instrument our own plugin (magicrew) to dump the first bad frame verbatim — that one I can change.

Landed in 538026e62, released in **v0.1.2962**. skygunner's patch is in, with your report as the case. When an error frame comes inside a 200, the status it names is the one the call fails at, rests at, and is booked at in Routing and Usage:

- a numeric `status` or `code` member from 400 to 599;
- otherwise "(HTTP 503)" or "（HTTP 503）" in the words, for 429 and 5xx only.

Your wps-lingxi 503 frame, mid-reply, now fails over as a 503 and shows 503 in Routing, where it showed 200, was rested as "other" and read "OK: …". A quoted string code ("429", "1113") is the vendor's own code, so it is not taken as a status. Words magpie wrote itself (the loop guard, an empty reply) name no status.

Left out of the patch: giving magpie's own error frames a code and status. Another magpie on the LAN would read its loop guard as a named 502.

Not tried: a real wps-lingxi account, or whether an AuditFailed counted as a 502 should rest the account. Leaving this open until you see it on your group.

One thing the fix does not reach, and it is every plugin we run.

`httpSaid` matches **only the bracketed form**:

```go
var httpSaid = regexp.MustCompile(`[(（]\s*HTTP\s*(429|5\d\d)\s*[)）]`)
```

Our five live plugins all write it **without** brackets:

| plugin | text it throws |
|---|---|
| loomy-auth | `"${what}返回 HTTP ${res.status}"` |
| officeace | `` `OfficeAce 目录读取失败：HTTP ${r.status}` `` |
| ima-local-auth | `` `ima: HTTP ${res.status} …` `` |
| today-plugin | `` `换 token 失败：HTTP ${res.status} …` `` |
| trustoken-auth | `` `HTTP ${res.status}` `` |

So `textStatus` returns 0 for every one of them, `namedStatus` returns 0, `carriedStatus` hands back the 200, and the frame is relayed as data exactly as before. **The only plugin that benefits today is wps-lingxi**, and only because it happens to write `（HTTP 503）` with full-width brackets — that is why my sample worked and the rest of the fleet does not.

**Suggestion, one line:** accept the bare form too, keeping the same narrow range:

```go
var httpSaid = regexp.MustCompile(`[(（]?\s*HTTP\s*(429|5\d\d)\s*[)）]?`)
```

The 429/5xx restriction is what makes it safe — a 4xx a message quotes is still ignored, per the comment above it. Two anchors are worth keeping, though:

- `"HTTP 500"` inside a quoted body the plugin pasted (`…上游返回 400：{"code":"InvalidArgument"}` has no HTTP word, but a vendor that echoes `HTTP 503` in its own message would now be read as the status)
- a plugin that says `HTTP 502` about *its own* upstream call, not about the reply that reached magpie

If you would rather not widen the regex, the alternative is the five plugins each moving to the bracketed form — five edits against one, and the next plugin written by someone else gets it wrong again. I would take the regex.

No PR from me (non-collaborator), so this is the diff in prose.

Live check on this machine, which is still on **0.1.2901** — the fix (`538026e62`, v0.1.2962) has not reached it yet, so this is the "before" side, and it is a second frame type from the same plugin:

```
2026-11-04 23:14:27  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=200
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：我还在不断学习中，暂时无法回答此问题，请尝试重新提问（上游审核未通过）（HTTP 502）
```

Two things worth noting:

1. **The frame names its status in the bracketed form** — `（HTTP 502）` with full-width brackets — which is exactly what `httpSaid` accepts. So this frame would be read as a 502 the moment v0.1.2962 is on the box; it is not a format problem like the five plugins I listed above. It was recorded as 200 only because the running build predates the patch.
2. **It is an AuditFailed, not a 503** — the same plugin's other error family. Your note says you did not try "whether an AuditFailed counted as a 502 should rest the account". This row is one of those: if it rests the account, a moderation refusal takes the account out of rotation for a request-level cause.

This machine has 2,036 calls since the 22:02 start: 2,023 at 200, 13 at 499 (agent cancelled), and this single 200-with-502. When I install ≥ v0.1.2962 I will re-run the same query and post the before/after.

Verified on 0.1.2971 (restarted 23:53:28). The before/after is clean.

**Same error shape, both sides of the restart.** Across 141,425 usage rows, 27 carry `（HTTP 5xx）` in `err`:

| when | rows | status booked |
|---|---|---|
| before 23:53:28 | 25 | **200 × 25** |
| after 23:53:28 | 2 | **503 × 1, 502 × 1** |

Two verbatim rows from after the restart (account masked):

```
2026-11-05T00:06:20  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=503  ms=42562  in=0 out=0
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常（上游暂时不可用，可重试）（HTTP 503）
  err_type=upstream_unavailable

2026-11-05T00:08:32  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=502  ms=13862  in=0 out=0
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：…（上游审核未通过）（HTTP 502）
```

The pre-restart twin of the second is the same sentence, 23:14:27 — booked `status=200`, `err_type=audit_blocked`, 316,783 upstream bytes. It read as a normal success.

**app.log agrees with the rows**, so the status is not a display artefact: `failed: 503 after 42.562s` at 00:07:03 (00:06:20.704 + 42.562s), and `failed: 502 after 13.862s` at 00:08:46.

**What I cannot show:** rest accounting. No line in the log after 23:53 mentions rest/cooldown, and the 502 request's three parallel attempts (10 ms apart, three accounts) all ended 499/502 — so no successful failover either. The status attribution is proven; the consequence is not.

Closing as verified. The bracket-form gap from my previous comment still stands as a separate finding — five live plugins write `HTTP N` without brackets.

Thanks for the follow-up and for checking the 502/503 bookings. I traced these five examples and exercised their error-producing functions through Magpie's plugin host and gateway. The ima inference example returns a real HTTP 502 before the stream; the other examples originate in account, catalog or token operations, so their status text is not necessarily the status of an inference stream. I would keep the existing bracketed/numeric handling rather than match every `HTTP 503` in message text, since that can also be quoted response content. If you have a different plugin version producing one of these errors inside an actual 200 SSE response, a redacted frame and Routing/Usage entry would help us check that specific path.

For clarity, four auxiliary-error fixtures intentionally invoke the original function from an adapter inference hook; only ima runs its real loader/chat/inference path. That proves transport of the thrown errors, not that each auxiliary function is normally called during inference. I used the publicly captured plugin sources, which may differ from your installed versions. The quoted-status control covers a pre-stream HTTP response, not all 200 SSE frames. These tests do not establish moderation cooldown or successful failover. No production code changed. AI-assisted investigation.

If you would rather not widen the regex, the alternative is the five plugins each moving to the bracketed form — five edits against one, and the next plugin written by someone else gets it wrong again. I would take the regex.

No PR from me (non-collaborator), so this is the diff in prose.

Live check on this machine, which is still on **0.1.2901** — the fix (`538026e62`, v0.1.2962) has not reached it yet, so this is the "before" side, and it is a second frame type from the same plugin:

```
2026-11-04 23:14:27  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=200
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：我还在不断学习中，暂时无法回答此问题，请尝试重新提问（上游审核未通过）（HTTP 502）
```

Two things worth noting:

1. **The frame names its status in the bracketed form** — `（HTTP 502）` with full-width brackets — which is exactly what `httpSaid` accepts. So this frame would be read as a 502 the moment v0.1.2962 is on the box; it is not a format problem like the five plugins I listed above. It was recorded as 200 only because the running build predates the patch.
2. **It is an AuditFailed, not a 503** — the same plugin's other error family. Your note says you did not try "whether an AuditFailed counted as a 502 should rest the account". This row is one of those: if it rests the account, a moderation refusal takes the account out of rotation for a request-level cause.

This machine has 2,036 calls since the 22:02 start: 2,023 at 200, 13 at 499 (agent cancelled), and this single 200-with-502. When I install ≥ v0.1.2962 I will re-run the same query and post the before/after.

Verified on 0.1.2971 (restarted 23:53:28). The before/after is clean.

**Same error shape, both sides of the restart.** Across 141,425 usage rows, 27 carry `（HTTP 5xx）` in `err`:

| when | rows | status booked |
|---|---|---|
| before 23:53:28 | 25 | **200 × 25** |
| after 23:53:28 | 2 | **503 × 1, 502 × 1** |

Two verbatim rows from after the restart (account masked):

```
2026-11-05T00:06:20  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=503  ms=42562  in=0 out=0
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AIError：AI服务异常（上游暂时不可用，可重试）（HTTP 503）
  err_type=upstream_unavailable

2026-11-05T00:08:32  wps-lingxi/kimi-k3.1-pro  status=502  ms=13862  in=0 out=0
  err: 灵犀上游返回 AuditFailed：…（上游审核未通过）（HTTP 502）
```

The pre-restart twin of the second is the same sentence, 23:14:27 — booked `status=200`, `err_type=audit_blocked`, 316,783 upstream bytes. It read as a normal success.

**app.log agrees with the rows**, so the status is not a display artefact: `failed: 503 after 42.562s` at 00:07:03 (00:06:20.704 + 42.562s), and `failed: 502 after 13.862s` at 00:08:46.

**What I cannot show:** rest accounting. No line in the log after 23:53 mentions rest/cooldown, and the 502 request's three parallel attempts (10 ms apart, three accounts) all ended 499/502 — so no successful failover either. The status attribution is proven; the consequence is not.

Closing as verified. The bracket-form gap from my previous comment still stands as a separate finding — five live plugins write `HTTP N` without brackets.

issue.title: A 200 whose body is an upstream billing error and whose usage is zero is recorded as success

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happens

magpie returns `HTTP 200` to the agent with a body that is an upstream billing error rather than a model answer. The routing record marks the request as fully successful — `status: 200`, `done: true`, `fail: null`, `err: null` — so magpie neither retries nor rotates to the next seat, and the body is delivered to the agent as if it were a completion.

Body shape observed (account identifiers and balances redacted; structure preserved verbatim):

```
Your subscription has expired.

API key status: expired
Name: <redacted>
USDT balance: <redacted> USDT
USDT spent: <redacted> USDT
exp_date: 2026-10-27T19:58:06.138Z
```

### Environment

- magpie `0.1.1696`, Windows (`magpie-windows-amd64.exe`)
- Provider: custom, OpenAI-compatible, base URL `https://api.qnaigc.com/v1`, model `qiniu/conatus-free`
- Consumer: an agent running through a magpie group (`group/pool`)

### Evidence

#### 1. Three consecutive attempts, three different response ids, byte-identical body

In a single session, three assistant messages (event seq 364, 372, 381) each carry:

| field | value |
|---|---|
| `replayState.response.responseModel` | `qiniu/conatus-free` |
| `responseId` (attempt 1) | `chatcmpl-ef4170fee13a44c4b8589a68d5d26e52` |
| `responseId` (attempt 2) | `chatcmpl-801e71111c404643a0023b085729d924` |
| `responseId` (attempt 3) | `chatcmpl-37e3c89dcad447258cae19b4e575168e` |
| `replayState.usage` | `{"inputTokens":0,"outputTokens":0,"totalTokens":0}` |
| `stopReason` | `stop` |

The three attempts produced the **same text, byte for byte**. Three distinct upstream response ids mean three real upstream calls, not a cached or replayed response.

#### 2. The routing log agrees: status 200, done, no usable `usage`

Filtering that day's `routing/2026-10-28.jsonl` on `served == "qiniu/conatus-free"`, 232 records were served by that seat between 00:02 and 09:26 +08:00 (I switched the provider off locally at 10:03). Six of them had this shape:

| local time (+08:00) | `tries[0].status` | `done` | `flow` | effective input tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 08:33:41.698 | 200 | true | 106 | 145,756 |
| 08:33:48.982 | 200 | true | 3 | 146,662 |
| 08:33:51.507 | 200 | true | 2 | 146,734 |
| 08:38:28.380 | 200 | true | 2 | 147,871 |
| 08:38:34.402 | 200 | true | 1 | 147,943 |
| 08:39:57.882 | 200 | true | 10 | 148,145 |

All six carry no usable `usage` — the field is absent or all zeros — and `tries[0].flow` is single- or double-digit, except one row at 106. So nothing in the record accounts for any generated token, while what reached the client was a short billing notice, not a completion.

I have not verified what `flow` counts, so I read it only as a very coarse size signal and do not propose it as a criterion.

#### 3. It happens only on large inputs, and only on this seat

Same day (00:00–10:03 +08:00, when I switched the provider off locally), requests with effective input (`prompt.tokens − usage[0].cache_read`) ≥ 120,000 tokens, grouped by `served`. "No usage" below means the record has no `usage` object, or one whose fields are all zero:

| `served` | large requests | of which no usage | success rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017` | 88 | 0 | 100% |
| `sn-deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` | 36 | 0 | 100% |
| `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` | 6 | 0 | 100% |
| `qiniu/conatus-free` | 14 | 10 | 28.6% |

Not all 10 are the shape in §2: six are the `200` + no usage + tiny `tries[0].flow` cases listed above, two had `tries[0].status == 402` (the first attempt on another seat was rejected and the request fell through to this one), and two produced a large `flow` (8,883 and 352). Counting only the six, this seat fails 6 of its 14 large requests.

Through the same client and the same proxy, all 130 large requests served by other seats that day carry token accounting (0 anomalies, sizes up to ~294K). So the trigger tracks this seat, not the request size or the request path — and large requests are demonstrably deliverable to other upstreams.

I can attach the redacted routing records (one line per anomaly) and the request payload if that helps.

### What magpie should do

Decide failure at magpie's own layer and rotate to the next seat instead of passing the body through. The signal is already in the record: an attempt that reports

- `status == 200`, **and**
- `usage` absent or `in + out + cache_read == 0`

produced no output tokens, so the body it returned cannot be the completion the client asked for; it should count as a failed attempt and the next seat tried. One false-positive class to guard against: providers that never report `usage` at all — for those the rule must stay off.

Today the body is a billing notice; next time it may be a quota page or a maintenance notice. Keying on the accounting rather than on the wording is what makes this hold.

### Why the consumer cannot work around it

The body arrives as a normal completion with `stopReason: "stop"` and a normal `responseId`, so on the consumer side there is no protocol-level signal to key on — only the text itself. Text heuristics are fragile and break on the next wording. An out-of-process watchdog that polls `routing/*.jsonl` can only react after the fact, with a delay window, and every poll cycle is a chance to miss.

The decision has to be made where the response is parsed: inside magpie.

### Workaround currently applied

We worked around it on this machine by switching that provider off (`magpie provider off qnaigc`), which removed the symptom here for a few hours but does not fix the failure class. It is currently re-enabled and placed last in its group, so large requests only reach it when the two seats ahead of it are unavailable.

### Related

- **#3948** — *Feature request: distinguish protocol errors and client-reported failures from HTTP success in request observability* (open, 2026-10-27). That one is the **reporting** side (make the request list tell the two apart). This issue is the **decision** side: a response of this shape must not count as a completed attempt, and must move to the next seat. Both are needed; neither replaces the other.

### Aside (a separate behaviour in the same area)

`magpie providers` reports `(none picked, so only the first 24)` for a provider whose `models` array is empty. An empty `models` list therefore does **not** mean "nothing exposed" — it means "unrestricted, first 24 shown". Worth a doc note or an explicit state, since it is easy to read as "off".

timeline.body:
Thanks for the follow-up and for checking the 502/503 bookings. I traced these five examples and exercised their error-producing functions through Magpie's plugin host and gateway. The ima inference example returns a real HTTP 502 before the stream; the other examples originate in account, catalog or token operations, so their status text is not necessarily the status of an inference stream. I would keep the existing bracketed/numeric handling rather than match every `HTTP 503` in message text, since that can also be quoted response content. If you have a different plugin version producing one of these errors inside an actual 200 SSE response, a redacted frame and Routing/Usage entry would help us check that specific path.

For clarity, four auxiliary-error fixtures intentionally invoke the original function from an adapter inference hook; only ima runs its real loader/chat/inference path. That proves transport of the thrown errors, not that each auxiliary function is normally called during inference. I used the publicly captured plugin sources, which may differ from your installed versions. The quoted-status control covers a pre-stream HTTP response, not all 200 SSE frames. These tests do not establish moderation cooldown or successful failover. No production code changed. AI-assisted investigation.

issue.title: [Bug] gateway: Claude Code's session-title request (output_config.format) gets an unstructured 200 from a custom provider, so the title never appears

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**What happens**

Claude Code's session-title request uses `output_config.format` (beta `structured-outputs-2025-12-15`) and expects a JSON object `{"title": "..."}`. Through magpie's gateway with a custom provider, the request returns **200 with plain text**, so Claude Code cannot parse a title and silently falls back to its derived session name / the terminal title `Claude Code`. No error is shown, which makes it look like Claude Code simply never names the session.

This is a different path from #4905: there the request is the Claude subscription interactive mode and is refused with 400. Here it is the generic gateway → custom provider translation, and the request is *accepted* but the schema is ignored.

**Environment**

- magpie `0.1.2851` (macOS, arm64; updated and gateway restarted, still reproducible)
- Claude Code `2.1.316`, pointed at `http://127.0.0.1:3425`
- Provider: a custom, Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible proxy (`new-api-deepseek`), model `new-api-deepseek/deepseek-flash[1m]`
- The same model is also the small/fast and haiku model, so it is what the title request uses

**Reproduction**

Claude Code sends this (the SDK converts the deprecated `output_format` to `output_config.format`):

```sh
curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3425/v1/messages?beta=true' \
  -H 'x-api-key: <key>' \
  -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \
  -H 'anthropic-beta: structured-outputs-2025-12-15' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "new-api-deepseek/deepseek-flash[1m]",
    "max_tokens": 256,
    "system": "Generate a concise title for this session.",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<session>\nhelp me add a herdr mod\n</session>"}],
    "output_config": {
      "format": {
        "type": "json_schema",
        "schema": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {"title": {"type": "string"}},
          "required": ["title"],
          "additionalProperties": false
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

Actual response (200):

```json
{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Add Herdr Mod"}],"model":"new-api-deepseek/deepseek-flash[1m]","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"end_turn","type":"message"}
```

Expected: the text block contains JSON matching the schema, e.g. `{"title": "Add Herdr Mod"}`.

Claude Code parses the text as JSON; plain text fails, it marks the title `unusable`, and retries on later turns while the session has no title.

**What I checked**

- Tested several models across providers through the Anthropic endpoint with the same body. Every one returned unstructured text:
  - `new-api-deepseek/deepseek-flash[1m]` → `Add Herdr Mod`
  - `new-api-deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` → `Title: "Request for Adding a Header Mod"`
  - `new-api/kimi-k3` → `**Adding a Herdr Mod**`
  - `new-api-gpt-anthropic/gpt-6-astra[1m]` → `Adding a Herd Mod`
  - `workbuddy-ai/max-model` → `Adding a Herdr Mod`
  - `workbuddy-ai/minimax-m3.1-flash` → `Adding a Herdr Mod`
- The OpenAI-shaped endpoints behave the same: `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `response_format: {"type":"json_schema", ...}` and `POST /v1/responses` with `text.format` also return plain text.
- `GET /v1/models` lists no model whose `supported_parameters` include `json_schema`/`response_format` (only `tools`, `tool_choice`, `reasoning`), so it looks like the gateway treats the capability as absent and drops the format rather than enforcing it.
- Claude Code's own session metadata (`~/.claude/sessions/*.json`) shows `nameSource: "derived"` (e.g. `xuxx-44`), never an auto title.

**Expected**

For a request that carries `output_config.format`, either:

1. translate it to the upstream's structured-output mechanism when the provider supports it (`response_format` for Chat Completions, `text.format` for Responses, `generationConfig.responseSchema` for Gemini), or emulate it (schema-constrained answer tool / validate-and-retry), or
2. if the provider cannot honor a schema, return a clear 400 instead of a 200 with unstructured text.

Silently returning plain text makes every client that relies on `output_config.format` get wrong data without any signal.

**Relation to #4905**

#4905 and its main-branch fix (`a25d3d081`, Claude subscription interactive mode via the bridge MCP answer tool) do not cover this path: here magpie is a gateway in front of a custom provider, not the interactive Claude Code runner, and no Claude account is involved.

**Suggestion**

At minimum, reject schema requests on providers that cannot honor them, so clients fail visibly; ideally translate or emulate the schema for the common Chat Completions path.
